counterexample: INSERT INTO INSTRUCTOR (ID, NAME, DEPT_NAME) VALUES (1, 'Instructor1', 'Dept1'); INSERT INTO COURSE (COURSE_ID, TITLE, DEPT_NAME, CREDITS) VALUES (101, 'Course1', 'Dept1', 3); INSERT INTO TEACHES (ID, COURSE_ID, SEC_ID, YEAR, INSTRUCTOR) VALUES (1, 101, 1, 2020, 1), (1, 101, 2, 2020, 1), (1, 101, 3, 2020, 1), (1, 101, 4, 2020, 1), (1, 101, 5, 2020, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 differ in how they handle the GROUP BY clause. Q1 groups by both YEAR and COURSE_ID, while Q2 only groups by YEAR. This difference affects the HAVING COUNT(ID) > 4 condition, leading to different results.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have multiple courses taught by the same instructor in the same year, with the count of such courses being exactly 4. This triggers the difference between Q1 and Q2.
